dedupe_keys.name: nhs england hospital surge capacity from covid 19 provision interventions march to may 2020

description: This case study calculates how much hospital capacity NHS England gained from the measures taken to treat COVID-19 patients between March and May 2020, and when elective surgery could resume. The authors, from Imperial College London, published it as an open-access journal article. They analysed NHS datasets and literature to estimate pre-pandemic capacity in general and acute beds, critical care beds, staff and ventilators, and quantified the effect of cancelling elective surgery, field hospitals, use of private hospitals, and deploying former and newly qualified medical staff. Coverage is England. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: capacity estimates rely on aggregate datasets and assumptions, staff availability was uncertain, and the analysis is specific to the first wave. The study found NHS England would not have had enough capacity in March and April 2020 without the interventions, which relieved shortfalls in critical care nurses, beds and junior doctors, and that elective surgery could run at normal levels only while no more than about 1,550 COVID-19 patients occupied critical care beds nationally, if the other measures were sustained. Simulation uses: parameterising hospital surge capacity and trade-offs with elective care in pandemic capacity planning. Related records: CPAS (case_study-cpas-uk-covid19-hospital-capacity-planning) forecast demand in the same period and CHIME (model-chime) is a simple surge model.
